tasks.short: Prepare and deliver a remedial learning programme

steps.what: Review pupil work and identify verified learning difficulties
Choose remedial objectives, methods and activities
Write the selected remedial activity instructions

loop.purpose: Phrase teacher-selected activities for the intended reading level
loop.input: Decided objectives, exact activities and teacher-specified vocabulary limits
loop.output: Draft instructions without new pedagogical decisions
loop.check: Teacher checks task meaning, omissions, examples, reading demand and alignment to selected objectives
loop.stop: Missing decisions or two failed revisions returns to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Native activity formats come first; variable instructions need wording adaptation

steps.what: Lay out the existing remedial worksheets and materials
Check all remedial materials and prepare physical teaching aids
Implement the remedial programme through direct teaching and adaptation

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} worksheet layouts before a bounded loop phrases the teacher's selected remedial activities. The teacher reviews actual pupil work in the pupil-record system {OTHER}, chooses the programme, checks the complete materials and retains all direct remedial teaching.
tasks.previous_blocker: Activity wording and repeated worksheet layout interrupt programme preparation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native layouts and bounded wording adaptation can reuse teacher-decided activities.
tasks.still_hard: The cause of a learning difficulty and the right intervention require professional judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees a pupil's response and adapts the intervention in the moment.
tasks.altitude: Pedagogical decisions and direct support stay with the teacher.

evidence.claim: LessonUp supports rewriting material at another level; it does not establish remedial diagnosis or this task's time saving.

assumptions: Boundary is preparation and delivery of an existing remedial programme using teacher-created worksheets, not a formal statutory support-plan approval. Existing pupil progress records are reviewed, not invented as a new trailing programme log.

s1 includes retrieval and manual interpretation of pupil work. s2 produces objective codes, selected activities, examples, reading level and intended sequence. The teacher captures these within retained work; no new assessment or structured diagnosis producer is assumed free.

Native layouts first. s3 retains 12 points for wording and source/meaning checks and repair; s4 removes only repeated worksheet arrangement. s5 retains full instruction/answer/accessibility review, manual layout repair and physical aids. More repair lowers the estimate; ordinary author saving stays retained and ungated.

No separate electronic material dispatch or new required record is established here. If the local programme requires a progress entry, actual parent message or formal plan release, add those actual steps and actions. Shares are provisional model estimates.
unknowns: Whether formal support-plan or parent-dispatch duties apply
research_questions: Does rewritten wording preserve the teacher-selected learning demand?
Observe material preparation separately from direct remedial instruction

already_counted.description: Wording/source checks, complete material review, layout repair and physical preparation.

incremental.description: Maintain activity drafting constraints and worksheet layouts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes three wording and ten layout points less one upkeep. Conservative unfamiliar learning need requires bespoke explanations and visual arrangements: only 0.8 wording and two recurring layout points disappear, giving 1.8 net. Programme selection and teaching retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign and grade routine class work and homework

steps.what: Choose and check the final class-work or homework assignment
Release the checked class-work or homework assignment to pupils
Collect returned pupil work and verify answer identifiers
Mark explicit closed-answer class-work and homework items
Judge open answers, check closed marks and write feedback
Total the teacher-checked assignment marks
Enter the actual assignment grade and feedback record
Check final assignment grades, feedback and pupil recipients
Release the checked assignment grades and feedback to pupils

tasks.design: Configure native {LMS} closed-item marking and score totals for routine practice assignments. The teacher still chooses the work, checks every mark, judges open answers, writes feedback and retains original record entry; assignment and feedback releases each have their own final-version gate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explicit answer-key comparisons and checked-mark totals are repeated manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Native fixed keys and arithmetic can draft these operations without model grading.
tasks.still_hard: Misconceptions, partial credit and meaningful feedback require teacher judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher understands why a pupil's answer is wrong or unexpectedly valid.
tasks.altitude: Assessment decisions stay with the teacher.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed closed-answer keys and arithmetic totals can be configured while open-answer grading remains with the teacher.

assumptions: Boundary is routine class work/homework, excluding the separate formal test cycle in task 6544. Do not count the same pupil response or grading action in both tasks. This scenario already uses an LMS with pupil-visible release controls.

s1 includes selecting and checking item identifiers, answer keys, rubric and pupil group. Pupils produce answers only after s2; s3 includes collection, identification, manual capture of non-digital answers and ambiguity repair. Missing or non-exact answers are graded manually in s5, not forced into deterministic matches.

Test native keys and total formulas first. s4 removes explicit key comparison only and s6 repeated arithmetic. s5 retains checking all closed marks, open-answer judgement and manual mismatch handling; s8 retains full totals/feedback/recipient review. More checking than these allowances lowers the estimate.

s7's original same-system grade record and ordinary save stay fully retained and ungated. s2 and s9 are actual pupil-visible releases, each separated and bound to its own complete final version; edits void the relevant approval. Both release points remain fully retained, with no saving for clicks.
Shares and upkeep are model estimates, not measured school figures. No model evaluates learning outcomes and no new pupil-data system is assumed.
unknowns: Closed-item share and current native marking use
Required assessment/privacy consultation and release permissions
research_questions: Test ambiguous but valid closed answers and verify manual fallback
Separate original record entry from any real second-system transfer

already_counted.description: Response capture, all mark checking, manual mismatches, original record entry and final feedback review.

incremental.description: Maintain checked answer keys and total formulas across assignment changes.

approvals.approved_version: s1 exact final assignment, answer setup and pupil group; any edit voids approval
s8 exact final grades, feedback and pupil recipients; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 20 key-comparison and ten arithmetic points less 1.5 upkeep. Conservative open-response-heavy homework leaves only four exact-key comparison and two total points reusable, giving six minus 1.5 = 4.5. Original entry, releases and feedback do not shrink.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare, administer and grade formal classroom tests

steps.what: Design test items, answer keys and evaluation criteria
Format the existing test paper and answer layout
Check the final test, instructions and intended pupil group
Issue the checked test to the intended pupils
Administer the test and collect identified pupil responses
Mark closed test items against the teacher-checked answer key
Grade open test answers and check all draft marks
Enter the original test result record
Check final test results, evaluation and pupil recipients
Release the checked test results to pupils

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} test layouts and exact-key draft marking in {LMS}. The teacher designs and checks the test, administers it, judges learning and records results; issuing the final test and releasing final results are separate gated actions with fully retained time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Test layout and exact-key marking repeat work that does not require original assessment judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document styles and fixed answer keys can handle these limited operations.
tasks.still_hard: Validity, partial credit, test conditions and interpreting progress remain pedagogical decisions.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher understands whether performance shows learning or an assessment flaw.
tasks.altitude: Assessment design and progress evaluation stay with the teacher.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: fixed test layouts and explicit answer-key matching can assist limited operations while teachers retain all assessment decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is a formal test cycle, disjoint from routine practice in task 6542. No test response or grading action is counted twice. The scenario already uses an LMS for test marks and pupil-visible release.

s1 produces item identifiers, original questions, key/rubric, layout constraints and intended pupil group. s5 includes administration, response collection, identity checking and manual entry of non-digital answers before s6. No new scanner, free response extraction or transferred capture is assumed.

Try native styles and exact keys first. s2 removes repeated layout only, not writing questions. s3 retains full test checking and manual layout repair. s6 removes explicit exact-key comparison only; s7 retains all mark checks, open/ambiguous answers and manual fallback. Extra repair beyond s3/s7/s9 reduces the estimate.

s8's original record entry and ordinary same-system save retain all five points and have no self-gate. s3 approves the complete test before s4; s9 approves complete results before s10. Edits void the corresponding approval. Actual issue and release time remains fully retained.
No AI scoring, level allocation or admission decision is introduced. Shares are provisional model estimates.
unknowns: Actual fixed-layout and exact-key marking time
Existing response capture and release workflow
research_questions: Does the layout preserve question grouping and accessibility?
Test unexpected correct responses and verify full teacher checking

already_counted.description: Test/layout review, response capture, all mark checking, manual fallback, original result entry and final review.

incremental.description: Maintain test layouts and checked answer-key configurations.

approvals.approved_version: s3 exact final test, instructions and intended pupil group; any edit voids approval
s9 exact final test results and pupil recipients; any edit voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes ten repeated-layout and ten exact-key comparison points less 1.5 upkeep. Conservative bespoke open-response test has custom diagrams and few closed questions: only two layout points and one comparison point disappear, leaving 1.5 net. Administration and learning evaluation retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Encourage exploration and perseverance for later grades

steps.what: Review current pupil learning goals and previous learning evidence
Choose suitable learning opportunities and challenging tasks
Encourage exploration and coach perseverance through challenging learning tasks

tasks.design: Configure a native current-goal view in the pupil-record system {OTHER} for context already reviewed by the teacher. The teacher chooses opportunities and personally encourages exploration and perseverance; no automated inference about motivation or emotions is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reviewing goals requires a little repeated record navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native pupil-goal views can shorten retrieval of existing context.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing when to encourage, change the task or allow productive struggle requires personal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher builds confidence and recognises what kind of support this pupil needs.
tasks.altitude: Direct encouragement and task selection stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys supports pupil records and learning-goal tracking, without establishing this task's time saving or automating encouragement.

assumptions: Boundary is encouragement using already available pupil goals and learning opportunities. Original assessment/record production belongs to its actual assessment task and is not claimed saved here. No new perseverance or motivation log is invented.

The teacher's existing assessed work supplies pupil identifier, goal code, current goal status and source work reference. s1 verifies and manually traces missing context. s2 selects existing opportunities; no free new catalogue or structured motivation data is assumed.

Native view first. Only 1.2 points of repeated navigation disappear from s1; 13.8 points of evidence reading, checking and fallback remain. Selection and conversation are fully retained. Actual written transition advice, record entry or sends must be added if required locally rather than hidden in encouragement.
Shares and upkeep are model estimates. No new personal-data capture or emotional classification is introduced.
unknowns: Whether a current-goal view already exists
Actual written transition duties, if any
research_questions: Can the native view preserve source-work references without hiding incomplete goals?

already_counted.description: Read and verify existing goal evidence and manually trace missing references.

incremental.description: Maintain current-goal view settings after record-field changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central removes 1.2 navigation points less 0.4 upkeep. Conservative transition to a new goal framework requires manual reference tracing and leaves only 0.6 point of existing-goal retrieval reusable, giving 0.2 net. All personal encouragement remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: A teacher who retains learning decisions and pupil relationships while reducing specific layout, exact-key comparison, totals and retrieval work.
skills_to_grow: Validate answer-key marking without overlooking valid alternatives
Check adapted instructions for learning demand
Separate internal record saves from actual pupil-visible releases
role.ambitious_version: Protect remedial instruction, fair assessment and encouragement while native tools handle demonstrable repeated preparation operations.
